implementation: Uncommitted working-tree changes; no deployment or hardware control changes.
scope: All five Rust crates: GPU backends/FFI, exporters and collectors, controls and profiles, TUI, unified CLI
NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and TPU paths; CPU/memory/disk/network/process/sensor telemetry
JSON contracts, Prometheus metrics, dashboard expressions, Nix release packaging and CI

findings.before: Locked Tokio and LRU versions had reported security/soundness advisories; unnecessary dependencies added size and maintenance exposure.
findings.implemented: Updated Tokio and Ratatui/LRU, upgraded sysinfo/libloading/reqwest/crossterm, removed protobuf/paste/color-eyre dependency paths, disabled unused default features. Final audit has zero findings.

findings.before: Capability probing called power-limit setters; even a dry run could write to a driver.
findings.implemented: Removed setter probes. Capability contract v2 reports available interfaces and limits; actual writes report permission errors. Mock NVML tests verify capabilities/dry-run make no writes.

findings.before: The insufficient-size code was incorrect and the legacy process symbol could be called with an incompatible structure.
findings.implemented: Use the correct return code, bounded count/query retries and v2/v3-compatible symbols; reject invalid or failed buffers. Added ABI and retry regression tests and matched live H100 process IDs against nvidia-smi.

findings.before: Failed bulk operations could report success; watts-to-milliwatts conversion could overflow.
findings.implemented: Propagate unsuccessful bulk results to a nonzero exit code and validate nonzero/checked multiplication before writes. Mock driver regression tests pass.

findings.before: Failed refreshes retained old telemetry; AMD indexing and Intel Sysman handle/counter assumptions were unsafe or misleading.
findings.implemented: Reset cached telemetry each refresh, check AMD frequency bounds, enumerate Sysman drivers separately and match UUIDs, guard Intel counter resets, omit unavailable live metrics. Pair NVML/AMD initialization with successful shutdown.

findings.before: The baseline Nix binary could not find gpu03 NVML without LD_LIBRARY_PATH.
findings.implemented: Added standard multiarch/lib64 driver locations. Updated binaries discover the H100 without an environment override.

findings.before: Repeated sysinfo construction and inventory scans increased cost; blocking collection delayed HTTP; standalone and unified exporter paths had diverged.
findings.implemented: Reuse system state, refresh slow inventory at most once per five seconds, share one server, run collection/encoding on at most four blocking workers, support IPv6 and both shutdown signals, reject zero intervals and explicitly unsupported features.

findings.before: Removed system devices and absent optional counters could leave stale series.
findings.implemented: Track previous disk/network/sensor labels and remove missing series; regression test covers disappearance.

findings.before: Process refresh/allocation ran unnecessarily, network rates assumed a fixed interval, UTF-8 slicing could panic, and errors could leave the terminal in raw mode.
findings.implemented: Refresh process detail only on its tab, select the top 30 before allocating names, use actual elapsed time and reset-safe counters, truncate by characters, and restore terminal state through RAII. Live PTY tests visit tabs and verify restoration.

findings.before: Using policy0 alone could advertise settings unsupported by other CPU policies.
findings.implemented: Intersect governors/EPP and common frequency bounds across all policies; synthetic policy regression test passes.

findings.before: HTTP clients were recreated and metric parsing could confuse labels/timestamps or create empty devices.
findings.implemented: Pool the client, bound request/connect timeouts, disable proxy/redirects, parse exact chip labels and finite metric values, ignore unknown metrics and support utilization fallback. Parser tests pass.

findings.before: The unified CLI omitted CPU/capabilities/apply and unavailable list telemetry appeared as zero.
findings.implemented: Share these control handlers between binaries, add parser coverage, and represent unavailable telemetry as JSON null/text N/A.

findings.before: Unused dependencies/default features and default release settings inflated shipped binaries.
findings.implemented: Enable thin LTO, one codegen unit and symbol stripping; trim dependency/features; extend CI with all-feature tests, strict Clippy, dependency audit and mock-driver contracts.

benchmarks.method: scripts/validate-hardware.py, release binaries, GPU plus system exporter, one-second collection interval, approximately 15 seconds per run. CPU time includes startup and shutdown; RSS is sampled once per scrape. Baseline and updated runs are sequential on active hosts.
interpretation: Single short runs are indicative, not statistically controlled performance guarantees.

Process counts/disks/system sensors now refresh at most once per five seconds; this intentionally reduces work versus the baseline one-second inventory scans. CPU/memory/network/GPU retain the requested interval.
Linux baseline needed LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; updated binaries did not.
H100 exporter mean scrape latency increased from 0.804 ms to 3.672 ms in these samples; report does not claim a latency improvement.
Metric line counts remained 406 on Mac and 108 on NVIDIA.
Last source change after benchmark binaries was an Apple helper cfg guard for Linux lint; it does not change runtime behavior.

validation.check: cargo audit --deny warnings and final JSON audit
Live NVML snapshot/process comparison with nvidia-smi
CLI list/info, exporter health/metrics/SIGTERM and PTY tab/terminal restoration
Unified exporter IPv6 health/shutdown, invalid interval and unavailable TPU feature errors
Read-only capabilities/dry-run behavior and mock control failure/overflow contracts

validation.result: passed; five packaging cases plus three Linux mock-driver cases

validation.check: nix flake check and portable release build
scripts/test-release.py against native portable release archive
Grafana dashboard JSON and metric expression references

compatibility_changes: Control JSON contract version is now 2: power_limit_settable describes interface/limit availability, not a write-permission probe.
Missing list temperature/power values are nullable.
SystemCollector::new now returns Result after the sysinfo upgrade.
Process/disk/system sensor inventory can lag by up to the next five-second refresh.
remaining_coverage_limits: AMD, Intel and TPU hardware was unavailable; code review, compilation and relevant tests do not establish live driver compatibility.
No real GPU power/clock/reset or CPU policy writes were executed on either host. Such writes were tested only where covered by mock/synthetic fixtures.
Only M4 Pro and H100 hardware was exercised; other GPU generations, multi-GPU/MIG configurations and device hotplug remain unverified.
Native macOS Nix packaging was exercised; other release architectures and Linux portability containers await CI.
Legacy NVML process v1-only symbols are deliberately unsupported to avoid an incompatible ABI call.
A holistic review and passing checks cannot prove absence of further defects.
